newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TENNIS-Steven's comeback at BellSouth Open.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-Steven's comeback at BellSouth Open.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Oct 31 - New Zealand tennis No 1 Brett Steven says he still has some way to go to full fitness as he recovers from a knee injury, NZPA reported on Thursday.
Steven hasn't played since withdrawing during New Zealand's Davis Cup loss to the Netherlands last month and is sitting out the rest of the year.
The 27-year-old Aucklander has targeted the BellSouth Open beginning on January 6 for his home-town comeback tournament.

It was at the same event this year that Steven reached an ATP singles final for the second time in his career, losing to Czech Jiri Novak during a rain-affected weekend that saw him get only a short break after a long three-set semifinal.
Steven said he had been doing mainly strength and fitness work in the gym but expected to be able to run again in a couple of weeks.
"It's been five or six weeks now since I picked up a racquet," he said on Wednesday.
"My knee is about 70 percent, but there is still a bit of time to go. I'm still having good days and bad days with it and it's a question of getting it more consistently good."
Steven said the enforced break had been frustrating. Tennis was his profession and, while he wasn't playing, there was no income.
But there were plus sides, such as being able to spend time with baby son Ryan and being more motivated for next year.
The inactivity has seen Steven's world ranking drop from the career-best 32 he achieved earlier this year to the high 90s and he is almost certain to need a wild card to get into the BellSouth Open.
He also faces the prospect of playing in more qualifying events than he has been used to in recent years.
"I've always played whichever tournament I've wanted, so it is going to be a big adjustment. But if I get myself fit and healthy, I'm determined to get my ranking back."
Steven has had a run of injuries over the past year or so, but said he expected to play a full schedule of tournaments again in 1997 to stay competitive.
Steven attended the launch of Auckland's summer of tennis, which included the announcement that Wimbledon finalist MaliVai Washington would return for a fifth time to start in the BellSouth Open.
The American, ranked 22nd in the world, has twice reached the last two in Auckland, and he will be the first Wimbledon finalist to play at Stanley St since New Zealander Chris Lewis in 1984.
Organisers also announced that two Austrians, 20th ranked Judith Wiesner and No 40 Barbara Schett, were confirmed for the ASB Bank Classic the week before the men's open.
The closing dates for entries for both tournaments are next month.
